ei.title: Chapter 5-13 Analysis: Speech: Communication, Not Performance
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute perfection in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human.

questions.passage: One of the ①<u>biggest</u> reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they ②<u>viewing</u> speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is ③<u>judging</u> them against a scale of absolute perfection in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that ④<u>communicates</u> the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: viewing → view: that절의 주어 they에 대한 본동사가 필요하므로 viewing이 아닌 view가 적절.
det.analysis:
① biggest — one of the + 최상급, 적절
② viewing — 원문은 view. 접속사 that이 이끄는 절의 주어 they에 대한 본동사가 필요 → view ←정답
③ judging — the audience is judging(현재진행), 적절
④ communicates — 선행사 address(단수) 수식 관계대명사절 동사, 적절
det.tip: 절의 본동사 자리에는 준동사(viewing)가 아닌 정동사(view)

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking ①<u>as</u> a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute perfection in which every misstated word or awkward gesture ②<u>will</u> count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that ③<u>communicate</u> the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him ④<u>seem</u> more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: communicate → communicates: 선행사 a well-thought-out address가 단수이므로 관계대명사절 동사는 communicates가 적절.
det.analysis:
① as — view A as B(A를 B로 여기다), 적절
② will — every ... will count(미래), 적절
③ communicate — 원문은 communicates. 선행사 address(단수)를 받는 that절 동사 → 3인칭 단수 communicates ←정답
④ seem — make + O + 원형부정사(seem), 적절
det.tip: 주격 관계대명사절 동사는 선행사(address 단수)에 수일치 → communicates

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is ①<u>judged</u> them against a scale of absolute perfection in ②<u>which</u> every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not ③<u>looking</u> for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually ④<u>enhance</u> a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: judged → judging: 뒤에 목적어 them이 있는 능동 진행(the audience is judging them)이므로 judging이 적절.
det.analysis:
① judged — 원문은 judging. the audience is judging them(능동 진행, 뒤에 목적어 them) → judging ←정답
② which — 전치사 in + 관계대명사, 적절
③ looking — are not looking(현재진행), 적절
④ enhance — 조동사 can + 동사원형, 적절
det.tip: 뒤에 목적어(them)가 있으면 능동(judging), be judged(수동)는 목적어를 못 가짐

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are ①<u>concerned</u> about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute perfection in ②<u>that</u> every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas ③<u>clearly</u> and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him ④<u>seem</u> more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: that → which: 전치사 in 뒤에는 관계대명사 that을 쓸 수 없으므로 in which가 적절.
det.analysis:
① concerned — be concerned about(~에 대해 걱정하는), 적절
② that — 원문은 which. 전치사(in) 바로 뒤에는 관계대명사 that을 쓸 수 없음(in that 불가) → in which ←정답
③ clearly — communicates ... clearly(동사 수식 부사), 적절
④ seem — make + O + 원형부정사, 적절
det.tip: 「전치사 + 관계대명사」에서는 that 불가 → in which

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are ①<u>concerned</u> about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute ②<u>perfection</u> in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas ③<u>clearly</u> and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually ④<u>reduce</u> a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 한두 개의 실수가 화자의 매력을 '떨어뜨리는(reduce)' 것이 아니라 '높이는(enhance)' 것이 문맥상 적절.
det.analysis:
① concerned — 걱정하는, 원문 일치
② perfection — 완벽함, 원문 일치
③ clearly — 명확하게, 원문 일치
④ reduce — 원문은 enhance(높이다). 실수가 화자를 더 인간적으로 보이게 해 매력을 '높인다'는 맥락 → enhance ←정답
det.tip: enhance(높이다) ↔ reduce(떨어뜨리다)

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a ①<u>mistake</u> in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute ②<u>imperfection</u> in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a ③<u>virtuoso</u> performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more ④<u>human</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 청중이 '절대적 완벽함(perfection)'의 기준으로 판단한다고 느끼는 맥락이므로 imperfection이 아닌 perfection이 적절.
det.analysis:
① mistake — 실수, 원문 일치
② imperfection — 원문은 perfection(완벽함). 화자는 청중이 '절대적 완벽함'의 잣대로 자신을 평가한다고 느낌 → perfection ←정답
③ virtuoso — 명연주의, 원문 일치
④ human — 인간적인, 원문 일치
det.tip: perfection(완벽함) ↔ imperfection(불완전함)

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute perfection in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human.
questions.stem: 사람들이 연설 실수를 걱정하는 이유 중 하나는 연설을 의사소통 행위가 아닌 공연으로 여기기 때문이다.

det.korean: they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication → 연설을 공연으로 여김.
det.analysis: T ←정답: 첫 문장 'they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication'에서 실수를 걱정하는 이유가 연설을 공연으로 보기 때문임을 직접 서술.
det.tip: view A as B rather than C = A를 C가 아닌 B로 여기다

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute perfection in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human.
questions.stem: 연설 청중은 바이올린 연주회의 심사위원처럼 완벽한 명연주를 기대한다.

det.korean: 청중은 심사위원 같지 않으며 명연주가 아니라 잘 정리된 연설을 원한다.
det.analysis: F ←정답: 본문 'speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital' 및 'not looking for a virtuoso performance'에서 청중은 명연주를 기대하지 않음을 서술.
det.tip: not like judges / not looking for a virtuoso performance = 명연주 기대 아님

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. questions.stem: 한두 개의 실수는 오히려 화자를 더 인간적으로 보이게 하여 매력을 높일 수 있다.

det.korean: an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human → 실수가 매력을 높일 수 있음.
det.analysis: T ←정답: 마지막 문장 'an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human'에서 직접 서술.
det.tip: enhance one's appeal = 매력을 높이다 / seem more human = 더 인간적으로 보이다

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of __________. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute perfection in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 연설을 '공연(performance)'이 아니라 '의사소통(communication)' 행위로 본다는 대조 구조.
det.analysis:
❌ ① performance — 공연 (앞의 a performance와 대조되는 단어여야 하므로 부적절)
❌ ② competition — 경쟁 (본문 맥락 없음)
✅ ③ communication — 의사소통 ←정답. 'a performance rather than an act of ______'의 대조 구조상 communication이 적절
❌ ④ celebration — 축하 (본문 맥락 없음)
det.tip: A rather than B 대조: a performance ↔ an act of communication

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute perfection in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a __________ address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 청중은 화자의 생각을 명확하고 직접적으로 전달하는, 즉 '잘 정리된(well-thought-out)' 연설을 원한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① well-thought-out — 잘 정리된 ←정답. 'communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly'와 연결
❌ ② technically flawless — 기술적으로 완벽한 (청중은 완벽함/명연주를 찾지 않음, 반대 맥락)
❌ ③ spontaneously delivered — 즉흥적으로 전달된 (본문 근거 없음)
❌ ④ emotionally overwhelming — 감정적으로 압도적인 (본문 근거 없음)
det.tip: 생각을 명확·직접 전달 → well-thought-out(잘 짜인) address

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute perfection in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 청중은 명연주가 아니라 화자의 생각을 clearly and directly 전달하는 연설을 원한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 사람들이 실수를 두려워하는 것은 연설을 '공연'으로 여기기 때문이지 '의사소통'으로 여겨서가 아님
❌ ② 본문은 청중이 심사위원과 '같지 않다(not like judges)'고 함
✅ ③ 본문: 'a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly' ←정답
❌ ④ 실수가 오히려 매력을 '높일' 수 있다고 함(always 떨어뜨림은 오류)
det.tip: 청중이 원하는 것 = 생각을 명확·직접 전달하는 연설

ch: 사람들은 연설을 의사소통 행위로 여겨서 실수를 두려워한다.
연설 청중은 아이스스케이팅 심사위원과 동일한 기준으로 평가한다.
청중은 화자의 생각을 명확하고 직접적으로 전달하는 연설을 원한다.
사소한 실수는 언제나 화자에 대한 청중의 호감을 떨어뜨린다.

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 본문은 실수 한두 개가 오히려 매력을 높일 수 있다고 하므로 '완전히 없애야만'은 불일치.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 본문: 'judging them against a scale of absolute perfection' — 일치
✅ ② 본문: 'not looking for a virtuoso performance' — 일치
✅ ③ 본문: 'every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them' — 일치
❌ ④ 본문은 'an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal'로 실수가 오히려 매력을 높일 수 있다고 함 → '완전히 없애야만'은 불일치 ←정답
det.tip: an error or two can enhance appeal → 실수를 완전히 없앨 필요 없음

ch: 실수를 걱정하는 사람들은 청중이 절대적 완벽함의 기준으로 자신을 판단한다고 느낀다.
연설 청중은 바이올린 연주회 같은 화려한 연주를 기대하지 않는다.
잘못 말한 단어나 어색한 몸짓이 감점 요인이 될 것이라고 화자는 두려워한다.
